title: GoOrganicAfrica Comoros calculator-readiness review — Batch 43

geography.note: Keep the three islands as top-level calculator regions. RGA-2 metadata supports lower geography including prefecture and commune, but detailed crop estimates and budgets must be validated before adding those selectors.

findings.detail: INSEED RGA-2 2025 results, based on the 2023/24 crop campaign, report 73,966 agricultural holdings, 89,282 ha of agricultural land and 56,576 ha cultivated. Average holding size is 0.40 ha and 85% of holdings operate less than 1 ha.
findings.interpretation: This is strong current structural evidence, but the small and fragmented holdings mean commercial-scale enterprise assumptions cannot be applied indiscriminately.

findings.detail: RGA-2 reports agricultural land of 44,561 ha on Ngazidja, 37,191 ha on Ndzuwani and 7,531 ha on Mwali. Mohéli has the highest share of holdings oriented toward sales at 32%, compared with 23% nationally.
findings.interpretation: Island segmentation is supported for land structure and market orientation; it is not yet sufficient to assign island-specific crop yields or costs.

findings.detail: RGA-2 reports national output of banana 72,809 t, cassava 59,149 t, sweet potato 11,684 t, vanilla 2,442 t, clove 2,178 t and ylang-ylang 355 t. Selected yields reported are mango 17.1 t/ha, lettuce 8.5 t/ha and cucumber 8.3 t/ha.
findings.interpretation: National campaign totals are not per-hectare yields. The three selected yield values require denominator, island, season and weighting checks against the detailed census tables before calculator use.

findings.detail: RGA-2 reports 49,679 livestock holdings, 270,571 poultry, 116,674 goats and 55,835 cattle.
findings.interpretation: National stock counts do not distinguish commercial broilers from layers or provide feed conversion, mortality, veterinary expenditure, sale prices or farm budgets.

findings.detail: Only 20% of cultivated land was reported as fertilized; within fertilized land, 54% used organic fertilizer, 29% mineral fertilizer and 17% a combination. Ten percent of crop producers reported phytosanitary product use. Census results also identify insufficient equipment (40%) and scarcity of improved seeds (38%) as reported constraints.
findings.interpretation: These are adoption and constraint indicators, not input quantities, application rates or prices. They cannot be converted into per-hectare costs.

findings.detail: INSEED NADA catalogue version 1.0 documents crop production Section F with island and prefecture identifiers, crop name and production unit. The data dictionary records a cleaned, weighted and validated dataset; access to anonymised microdata is controlled by application and research-purpose commitments.
findings.interpretation: The public metadata establishes a credible extraction route but is not itself numeric microdata. Request access or obtain the published weighted island/prefecture tables; do not infer values from raw sample counts.

findings.detail: The World Bank Real Time Food Prices global catalogue version 2026-10-05 lists 37 countries and 3,181 markets, but Comoros is not among the listed country economies.
findings.interpretation: Do not claim that the World Bank October 2026 RTFP dataset supplies Comoros market prices. A Comoros-specific WFP/FAO/Ministry/market series remains to be located and validated.

findings.detail: FAO's 2025 Comoros technical report analyses a 2021 household survey and provides historical production/yield context.
findings.interpretation: Use as a methodological and historical cross-check only; the 2023/24 RGA-2 is the newer structural source.

readiness.calculator_mapping_and_test_cases: blocked_no validated island crop budget inputs or regression cases

outstanding: Obtain INSEED-authorised RGA-2 microdata access or published weighted tables.
Extract island/prefecture/crop/season area, production, harvested area and yield with survey weights and definitions.
Find dated local producer/farmgate prices by island, crop, grade, unit and market; do not substitute retail prices.
Obtain farmer-paid seed, fertilizer, organic amendment and crop-protection prices and application rates.
Collect labour, irrigation, water, energy, machinery hire, land preparation, packaging, storage and transport costs.
Build separate smallholder enterprise budgets reflecting the 0.40 ha average holding and island market orientation.
Validate livestock species and production systems, especially broiler/layer distinction, feed, mortality, veterinary and output prices.
Map the evidence to the current 17 calculator commodities only where crop identity and production system match; do not force banana, vanilla, clove or ylang-ylang into unrelated profiles.
safeguards: No national crop total converted into a yield without a matching harvested-area denominator.
No controlled microdata assumed to be publicly downloaded or accessed.
No retail or imported-food price reclassified as a farmgate price.
No input-use percentage converted into a per-hectare input budget.
No national average applied to every island without evidence.
No calculator profile or formula activated or changed.
conclusion: Comoros has a substantially improved and current census evidence base, including selected yields, island-level land structure and documented microdata fields. However, farmgate prices, farmer-paid input costs and island-specific enterprise budgets are not yet validated. Retain research-only status.
